deep.reconstruction:
Folio 179v is part of the introduction to a lecture course on number theory, probably Riemann's own notes for the lecture. It continues the historical sketch from 179r (Fermat, Euler, Lagrange, Legendre, Gauss). There is almost no mathematics on the page; it is methodological and historical prose, then the first definition.

(1) Historical and methodological remarks.
- Gauss's Disquisitiones Arithmeticae present the theory coherently, but in so extremely compressed a way that it is hardly understood. The words naming a further authority and the number '207' are unclear; they look like a reference.
- Number theory is called an independent (or 'simplest') discipline. It has entered into connection with other disciplines, namely integral calculus, (probably) the theory of series or cyclotomy, and higher algebra.
- It is difficult but very interesting, so the aim is to make its theorems more and more accessible.
- No history of the science can be given until one knows the science fully in its essential results.
- The theory has the advantage that it connects directly to the first elements and yet soon leads to difficult results.

(2) Foundations.
- The concept of number is so widespread (or elementary) that it is very hard to define, so the (positive) integers are presupposed.
- The lecturer starts from the generation of numbers by multiplication, defined through addition: a×b means a taken b times as a summand, a×b = a + a + ... + a (b terms). a is the multiplicand and b the multiplier.
- The last line ('Diese Zahlen, deren Werth ist von-') continues on the next page as 'unabhängig von der Ordnung': the value does not depend on the order.
- The next page then proves commutativity and associativity by counting a rectangular array of a's. Writing the array (ab)c with all entries 1 gives bc = cb. This is my inference from the next page and is not shown on this one.
errors: No mathematical errors. The only formal content is the standard definition a×b = a+...+a (b summands).

results.what: Definition of multiplication of positive integers as repeated addition (a×b = a added b times; multiplicand, multiplier)
results.modern_name: Recursive/iterated-addition definition of multiplication on N
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (Euclid Elements VII Def. 15); formalized by Grassmann 1861 and Dedekind/Peano

results.what: Methodological remark that Gauss's Disquisitiones are too compressed, and that number theory is linked with integral calculus and higher algebra

deep.surprise_reason: Introductory lecture remarks and the elementary definition of multiplication as repeated addition. This is entirely standard material for an introductory number-theory course of the 1850s.

checkable.sympy: a, b = 3, 5; a*b == sum([a for i in range(b)])
checkable.asserts: a×b equals a added b times (instance)
The sum of b copies of a equals a*b (symbolic)

transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'ist so weit[?]' is more likely 'ist so äußerst gedrängter Weise dargestellt'.
Line 2: 'wie Baentsch[?] & Prüfungen[?] 207' is very uncertain. It seems to name an authority or reference with a number; I cannot read it reliably.
'Geschäftsmann[?] einfachste Disciplin' probably begins with 'Zahlentheorie' (or 'Seitdem'), e.g. 'Zahlentheorie ... selbständige/einfachste Disciplin'.
'& von Disciplinen in Verbindung getreten' is better read 'mit [anderen] Disciplinen in Verbindung getreten'.
'Buchstaben-' (twice) looks more like 'Reihenlehre' (or possibly 'Kreistheilung'): 'namentl. mit der Reihenlehre, Integralrechnung, Reihenlehre und höheren Algebra'. Uncertain.
'Darum[?] schwierig' is possibly 'Zahlentheorie schwierig' or 'Daher schwierig'.
'Eine Geschichte der Wiss. in Verbindung' is likely 'Keine Geschichte der Wiss. zu geben' (no history can be given until the science is known). 'in Verbindung' is doubtful.
'(wie ich hab[?])' is possibly '(wie ich hoffe)'.
'Dagegen erst angefangen' is probably 'Daher erst angefangen'.
'Die ganze Zahlen vorausgesetzt' should read 'Die ganzen Zahlen vorausgesetzt'.
